original_value: The heart is the organ that pumps blood with oxygen and nutrients into all body organs by a rhythmic cycle overlapping between contraction and dilatation. This is done by producing an audible sound which we can hear using a stethoscope. Many are the causes affecting the normal function of this most vital organ. In this respect, the heart sound classification has become one of the diagnostic tools that allow the discrimination between patients and healthy people; this diagnosis is less painful, less costly and less time consuming. In this paper, we present a classification algorithm based on the extraction of 20 features from segmented phonocardiogram “PCG” signals. We applied four types of machine learning classifiers that are k- Near Neighbor “KNN”, Support Vector Machine “SVM”, Tree, and Naïve Bayes “NB” so as to train old features and predict the new entry. To make our results measurable, we have chosen the PASCAL Classifying Heart Sounds challenge, which is a rich database and is conducive to classifying the PCGs into four classes for dataset A and three classes for dataset B. The main finding is about 3.06 total precision of the dataset A and 2.37 of the dataset B.

result.paraphrase: The heart is the organ that circulates oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood to all body organs through a rhythmic alternation of contraction and relaxation. Its action produces audible sounds that can be heard with a stethoscope. Because many factors can disrupt the normal function of this vital organ, heart sound classification has become a diagnostic tool for distinguishing patients from healthy people, offering a less painful, less expensive, and less time-consuming diagnosis. In this paper, we propose a classification algorithm that extracts 20 features from segmented phonocardiogram (PCG) signals. We used four machine learning classifiers—k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Tree, and Naïve Bayes (NB)—to train on existing features and predict new entries. For measurable results, we selected the PASCAL Classifying Heart Sounds challenge, a rich database suitable for classifying PCGs into four classes for dataset A and three classes for dataset B. The main result is a total precision of about 3.06 for dataset A and 2.37 for dataset B.
